text.p: Italian bond futures held to higher levels in late afternoon ahead of a second round of preliminary February CPI inflation data, after the market was helped earlier by Thursday's CPI figures and a slightly stronger lira.

Six Italian sample cities' data late Thursday pointed to February Italian CPI inflation running at 2.2-2.3 percent year on year against 2.6 percent previously. February's monthly CPI was seen flat after January's month on month rate of 0.2.
A further five cities Turin, Florence, Naples, Bari, and Palermo are scheduled to report their preliminary Feb CPI figures at 1630 GMT this afternoon.
"The market liked the figures last night, and a confirmation of the lower inflation trend could support further gains," said one trader on London's LIFFE market.

Eurostat, the EU office responsible for overseeing national government's accounting practices, gave its approval to Italy's one-off Eurotax for 1997. Although largely expected by the market, dealers said it helped lend some support.
Dealers added the Italian market was forging its own way today focusing on the CPI numbers and lira, and was largely ignoring the slightly lower trend of bunds and U.S. T-bonds.
